decisions.statement: An initiative is assigned from the menu the editor draws over that row.
An initiative row is offered the assign item the manifest hangs on the work view.
No row that is no initiative is offered that item.
A row's initiative is read off that row by the module deleting an initiative.
A row that is no initiative assigns nothing.
Whether that seat takes the initiative is settled by the command rather than here.
The seat an initiative goes to is named by the module naming that seat off the slug.
That seat is named here for the panel to hold the initiative in that seat's color.
The panel is told an initiative is being assigned before the command is called.
The panel is told the landing answered once the command answers.
The panel is told the initiative stayed where the command is refused.
A refusal saying that seat answers to that initiative already is told that same way.
The panel's watch is handed in rather than imported.
Whether that seat is available is settled by the command rather than here.
The command's first line is shown to Alan, and every line is written to the channel.
An assignment that failed is said to Alan once and written to the panel's channel.
An assignment waits the ceiling the harness names rather than a ceiling named here.
The editor is handed in rather than imported.
The harness call is handed in rather than imported.
The command asked is named by reading the slug off that command's own page.
A refusal saying a body moved between the read and the write is said to Alan as one sentence.
That refusal is known by the module knowing a drop's refusal.
Every other refusal reaches Alan in the words that refusal was made in.
Alan is not asked to confirm before an initiative is assigned.
Nothing here writes a seat's page.
Nothing here draws a row.
Nothing here reads a color or reads the fleet.

definition: the initiative Alan assigns in the work tree named to the command and to the panel holding it
